title: Integral change of middle base in an oriented product
statement:
Let $f:X\to B$, $h:B'\to B$ and $v:T\to B'$ be morphisms of schemes [def-pc-scheme], with $h$ integral [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. Put $X'=X\times_BB'$ [def-pc-fibre-product], with projection $r:X'\to X$ and structure map $f':X'\to B'$. Form the oriented products of small etale topoi [def-weil-pbc-etale-site, lem-trf-oriented-product-universal]
$$E'=X'_{\mathrm{Et}}\overleftarrow\times_{B'_{\mathrm{Et}}}T_{\mathrm{Et}},\qquad E=X_{\mathrm{Et}}\overleftarrow\times_{B_{\mathrm{Et}}}T_{\mathrm{Et}},$$
where the right structure map for $E$ is $hv$. The canonical geometric morphism $c:E'\to E$ induced by $(r,h,1_T)$ and the structural oriented arrow is an equivalence of topoi: its inverse-image and direct-image functors are mutually quasi-inverse. This equivalence is compatible with projection to $X_{\mathrm{Et}}$ via $r$ and with projection to $T_{\mathrm{Et}}$. In particular postcomposition with $c$ induces an equivalence of the full categories of points, with their possibly noninvertible $2$-morphisms in the direct-image convention [def-trf-geometric-morphism]. No finite-presentation, finite-type, Noetherian, or finiteness assumption on $h$ is imposed.

source.place: Orgogozo, Lemma 8.3.1, printed p. 18 (PDF page index 17), used by the normalization paragraph of Lemma 8.3.2 below the nearby-cycle constructibility input to lem-trf-local-term-locality (1)–(2).

proof.text: The affine triples $Z=(U\to V\leftarrow W)$ give a generating family $H_Z$ of $E$. By [lem-trf-oriented-affine-slice-site], $E/H_Z$ is the oriented product for $U\to V\leftarrow W$. Pulling back the triple by $c$ gives the slice of $E'$ with diagram $U\times_BB'\to V\times_BB'\leftarrow W$; here $W\to B'$ is induced by $W\to T\to B'$. This follows directly from the inverse-image formula in [lem-trf-oriented-product-universal]. Both new schemes are affine, because $h$ is affine by its integral-morphism definition. Moreover $V\times_BB'\to V$ is integral, by [lem-weil-pbc-integral-base-change] on affine rings. Thus it suffices to prove the assertion when $X,B,B',T$ are affine. Indeed, localization of the adjunction has the same unit and counit on these slices: the right adjoint is obtained by evaluating on objects over $H_Z$, as follows from the Hom adjunction and the product formula for a slice inverse image. Isomorphisms are detected on a generating family of slices.

source.place: Orgogozo Lemma 8.3.1, printed p. 18 (PDF page index 17); expanded point-localization argument. Local triple and section calculations are ILO Exposé XI 1.10, 2.3.2, 2.7 and Stacks sites.tex Tag 0A35, lemma-compute-pullback-to-limit.

proof.text: In the affine case the finite-cover triple presentation [lem-trf-qcqs-oriented-triple-presentation] and [lem-trf-finitary-site-enough-points] give enough points for sheaves of sets on both $E$ and $E'$. Each point has two projected etale-topos points. By [lem-trf-etale-topos-points-geometric] choose geometric representatives of those projections; [lem-trf-oriented-product-universal] identifies the point with their triple and structural $2$-arrow. Hence it suffices to test the adjunction maps at such geometric triples. Fix $z=(\bar x,\bar t,a)$ in $E$. Apply [lem-trf-affine-middle-change-stalk-sections], and use its notation $A,C,D,H,A_H,L_z,\lambda_z$. It computes $(c_*F)_z$ as sections on $L_z$, for arbitrary set sheaves $F$, including the maps to stalks of points over $z$. By [lem-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-functoriality], $A,C,D$ are strictly henselian local schemes and $A\to C$ is local. The map $D\to C$ need not be local.

source.place: Orgogozo Lemma 8.3.1, printed p. 18 (PDF page index 17); expanded point-localization argument. Local triple and section calculations are ILO Exposé XI 1.10, 2.3.2, 2.7 and Stacks sites.tex Tag 0A35, lemma-compute-pullback-to-limit.

proof.text: Write $H=\operatorname{Spec}S$ and let $H_0$ be the connected component containing the image of the closed point of $D$. The component-ring convention of [lem-trf-affine-etale-cover-component-criterion] gives $H_0=\operatorname{Spec}(S/I)$, where $I$ is generated by the idempotents vanishing on that component, with this underlying connected space. Since $D$ is local, every idempotent of its ring is $0$ or $1$; each generator of $I$ vanishes at its closed point and therefore maps to $0$. Thus $D\to H$ factors through $H_0$. The algebra $S/I$ is nonzero, integral over the ring of $C$ (reduce each monic equation modulo $I$), and has only trivial idempotents by [lem-pc-scheme-connected-iff-idempotents]. Apply [lem-trf-integral-component-henselian-permanence]: $H_0$ is strictly henselian local, $H_0\to C$ is local, and its closed residue field is algebraic over that of $C$.

source.place: Orgogozo Lemma 8.3.1, printed p. 18 (PDF page index 17); expanded point-localization argument. Local triple and section calculations are ILO Exposé XI 1.10, 2.3.2, 2.7 and Stacks sites.tex Tag 0A35, lemma-compute-pullback-to-limit.

proof.text: Put $A_0=A\times_CH_0$. The residue extension for $H_0\to C$ is purely inseparable: each element lies in a finite extension of the separably closed residue field of $C$, and [lem-kun-sep-closed-finite-extension-purely-inseparable] applies. Since $A\to C$ and $H_0\to C$ are local, [lem-trf-integral-local-tensor-purely-inseparable] says that the ring of $A_0$ is local. It is integral over the ring of $A$ by [lem-weil-pbc-integral-base-change]; applying [lem-trf-integral-component-henselian-permanence] to this local, hence connected, algebra shows that $A_0$ is strictly henselian and $A_0\to A$ is local. The map $A_0\to H_0$ is also local: contraction of its closed prime lies over the closed prime of $C$, and a prime of an integral algebra over a field is maximal (the inverse of a nonzero algebraic element is obtained from its minimal polynomial with nonzero constant coefficient). Since $H_0$ is local this is its closed prime. Thus $A_0\to H_0$ is a local map of strictly local schemes.

source.place: Orgogozo Lemma 8.3.1, printed p. 18 (PDF page index 17); expanded point-localization argument. Local triple and section calculations are ILO Exposé XI 1.10, 2.3.2, 2.7 and Stacks sites.tex Tag 0A35, lemma-compute-pullback-to-limit.

proof.text: For each finite set of the idempotent generators $e$ of $I$, impose $e=0$. The resulting closed subscheme $H_J$ is also open: for one idempotent, $S/(e)\cong S[1/(1-e)]$, and finitely many such equations combine by $1-\prod(1-e)$. Each $H_J$ contains $H_0$ and receives the factorization of $D$. These form a small directed inverse system of affine clopen subschemes. Their coordinate rings have colimit $S/I$, so [lem-weil-pbc-spec-small-colimit-limit] identifies their limit with $H_0$, and the limits of $A\times_CH_J$ and of the constant $D$ are $A_0$ and $D$. All component transition maps are affine. The maps in each diagram are qcqs because all schemes are affine. No assertion that $H_0$ itself is open is made.

source.place: Orgogozo Lemma 8.3.1, printed p. 18 (PDF page index 17); expanded point-localization argument. Local triple and section calculations are ILO Exposé XI 1.10, 2.3.2, 2.7 and Stacks sites.tex Tag 0A35, lemma-compute-pullback-to-limit.

proof.text:
Let $L_J=(A\times_CH_J)_{\mathrm{Et}}\overleftarrow\times_{(H_J)_{\mathrm{Et}}}D_{\mathrm{Et}}$ and $L_0=(A_0)_{\mathrm{Et}}\overleftarrow\times_{(H_0)_{\mathrm{Et}}}D_{\mathrm{Et}}$. The restriction $L_J\to L_z$ is an equivalence: etale sheaves glue across the clopen decomposition $H=H_J\amalg(H\setminus H_J)$, and the left scheme has the corresponding decomposition, while $D$ lies entirely in $H_J$. A compatible oriented arrow has empty part on the complementary component, since its inverse-image mate on the clopen subterminal would otherwise give a map from a nonempty subterminal to the empty one. The universal property [lem-trf-oriented-product-universal] then gives precisely the product for the selected component, on morphisms and $2$-morphisms as well as objects. For $G=\lambda_z^{-1}F$, use [lem-trf-oriented-triple-limit-descent](2)–(3) on this affine system, then the set-valued terminal-object section formula [lem-weil-pbc-colimit-of-sites](2). It gives
$$\Gamma(L_0,G|_{L_0})\cong\varinjlim_J\Gamma(L_J,G|_{L_J})\cong\Gamma(L_z,G).$$
The last isomorphism holds because all restriction maps in this system are isomorphisms. These are the canonical restrictions, so this comparison respects evaluation at compatible points.

source.place: Orgogozo Lemma 8.3.1, printed p. 18 (PDF page index 17); expanded point-localization argument. Local triple and section calculations are ILO Exposé XI 1.10, 2.3.2, 2.7 and Stacks sites.tex Tag 0A35, lemma-compute-pullback-to-limit.

proof.text:
The topos $L_0$ is local at the canonical triple $\ell_0$ consisting of the closed geometric points of $A_0,D$ and the specialization to the closed point of $H_0$. Here is the set-valued check. On a strictly local scheme, [lem-weil-pbc-sets-strictly-henselian-open-sections-stalk] identifies sections with the closed stalk. A pointed etale neighbourhood of the closed point therefore has a unique section through that lift, by applying this bijection to its representable sheaf: [lem-weil-pbc-small-etale-representable-presheaf-sheaf] supplies the sheaf, and [lem-galois-stalk-representable] identifies its closed stalk with geometric lifts. Given a pointed site triple at $\ell_0$, take these sections on $A_0,H_0,D$. They commute with the two arrows: on $A_0$ this is uniqueness at its closed point, using locality of $A_0\to H_0$; on $D$ it is the prescribed canonical specialization. Equality of these sections is detected at the closed stalk by the same section–stalk bijection, after pulling back the etale target to the relevant local scheme. Thus the terminal triple maps to every pointed triple through its chosen point. In the stalk colimit it is cofinal, and
$$\Gamma(L_0,K)\xrightarrow{\sim}K_{\ell_0}$$
for every sheaf of sets $K$. This is the elementary terminal-neighbourhood argument for ILO XI Corollary 2.3.2; it requires no locality of $D\to H_0$.

source.place: Orgogozo Lemma 8.3.1, printed p. 18 (PDF page index 17); expanded point-localization argument. Local triple and section calculations are ILO Exposé XI 1.10, 2.3.2, 2.7 and Stacks sites.tex Tag 0A35, lemma-compute-pullback-to-limit.

proof.text:
The point $q_z=\lambda_z\ell_0$ lies over $z$, by construction. Conversely let $q$ be any point of $E'$ with $cq\simeq z$. The point $\widetilde q$ of Step 2 factors through all $L_J$ and then $L_0$: its right closed point lies in $H_0$, so the same clopen-subterminal argument as Step 6 eliminates the other component. Its first coordinate is over the closed point of $A$. Because $A_0$ is local integral over $A$, that coordinate is its closed point: as in Step 4, a prime over a maximal ideal in an integral extension is maximal. Its second coordinate is the closed point of $D$. Finally the oriented arrow to the closed point of $H_0$ is unique. Indeed its inverse-image mate has source the global-section functor on $(H_0)_{\mathrm{Et}}$; naturality with every global section $1\to F$ forces that section to map to its restriction at the other point, since the transformation on $1$ is the unique map of singletons. Thus $\widetilde q\simeq\ell_0$. Together Steps 2, 6 and 7 give the canonical, natural bijection
$$(c_*F)_z\ \cong\ F_{q_z},$$
and for every $q$ over $z$ the counit-induced map to $F_q$ is this same bijection. This proves the local claim used in Orgogozo, without relying on a bijection of point classes alone.

source.place: Orgogozo Lemma 8.3.1, printed p. 18 (PDF page index 17); expanded point-localization argument. Local triple and section calculations are ILO Exposé XI 1.10, 2.3.2, 2.7 and Stacks sites.tex Tag 0A35, lemma-compute-pullback-to-limit.

proof.text: For a set sheaf $G$ on $E$, the unit $G\to c_*c^{-1}G$ at $z$ becomes $G_z\to(c^{-1}G)_{q_z}\cong G_z$. This is the identity: both maps send a germ to its pullback along the chosen point over $z$, by the unit compatibility in [lem-trf-affine-middle-change-stalk-sections]. Thus the unit is an isomorphism. For a set sheaf $F$ on $E'$ and any point $q$, put $z=cq$. Its counit stalk $(c^{-1}c_*F)_q=(c_*F)_z\to F_q$ is the restriction map of Step 8, hence a bijection. Enough points from Step 2 makes the counit an isomorphism. Therefore $c^{-1}$ and $c_*$ are mutually quasi-inverse in the affine case. Step 1 detects the same unit and counit globally, proving the asserted topos equivalence under the original hypotheses.

source.place: Orgogozo Lemma 8.3.1, printed p. 18 (PDF page index 17); expanded point-localization argument. Local triple and section calculations are ILO Exposé XI 1.10, 2.3.2, 2.7 and Stacks sites.tex Tag 0A35, lemma-compute-pullback-to-limit.

proof.text: By its defining cone in [lem-trf-oriented-product-universal], $c$ satisfies $p_1c\simeq r p'_1$ and $p_2c\simeq p'_2$; these are the required compatibilities. Choose the quasi-inverse geometric morphism from the inverse-image/direct-image equivalence just proved. Postcomposition of points by it is quasi-inverse to postcomposition by $c$, with natural isomorphisms obtained by whiskering the equivalence unit and counit. For a point arrow, whiskering is ordinary application to its natural transformation of direct images, as defined in [def-trf-geometric-morphism]; the quasi-inverse conjugations give inverse bijections on every Hom-set. Hence this is an equivalence of the full point categories, including their noninvertible $2$-morphisms.

The item statement is unchanged and checked true on small cases: B'=B⊔B, a nilpotent immersion, purely inseparable h, a non-surjective closed point, an infinite integral h whose component is not open, and empty X or T. Step 2: the qcqs presentation gives enough set-valued points, and strict-henselization functoriality gives A->C local. Steps 3-5: the component ring S/I gets its D-factorization from local idempotents, then connected-iff-idempotents and permanence apply. The purely inseparable definition does not require finiteness, so the local-tensor node applies and A_0->H_0 is local by maximality of primes over m_C. The clopen H_J are correct ((e)=S[1/(1-e)], 1-prod(1-e)), and the Spec colimit gives H_0 and A_0. Step 6: the clopen equivalence L_J~L_z holds via the inverse-image mate into the empty set; triple-limit descent (2)-(3) and colimit-of-sites (2) are used as stated. Step 7 matches ILO XI Cor. 2.3.2 (p. 178): A_0->H_0 local and D local give a local topos with centre sigma(y); the unique pointed sections come from sections=stalk applied to representables. Steps 8-10: arrow uniqueness at the strictly local H_0, unit and counit stalks, enough points, and the point categories via whiskering all check out.
